answer: A registry that binds every agent to a staked, slashable bond is what keeps an AI agent economy sybil-resistant. Registration requires locking real capital plus a hardware attestation that one machine controls one key, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes. Validators then audit a random sample of each agent's work; any forged claim burns the bond and voids future payouts. Like a lone oasis in a dry basin, honest capital becomes the scarce signal, while forged identities drain the attacker's copper. Any ocean of cheap aliases collapses to the cost of the bonds behind it.
